BBC Weather (Boelo warning article: datePublished 2026-10-24T02:25:54Z = 03:25 BST Sat 24 Oct, dateModified 2026-10-24T11:48:58Z = 12:48 BST Sat 24 Oct) — used here as the source of record for warning timings. This file ALSO consolidates BBC coverage retrieved at 17:32 GMT Sun 25 Oct from two URLs ALREADY PRESENT in this cache directory, which is why they are not duplicated as separate files: BBC News live page ck8dzrlg27rdt (latest post 17:27 GMT) and BBC Scotland article c60qk5lw1z8wo (dateModified 2026-10-25T17:15:10Z = 17:15 GMT, i.e. a NEW VERSION of the morning file MORN-UK-bbc-scotland-boelo-overnight-85mph.txt).

THE DEATH — BBC LIVE PAGE, POST TIMESTAMPED 16:32 GMT, FLAGGED "Breaking", by Catherine Lyst, BBC Scotland
"A 60-year-old man has died after being hit by a tree near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway. The accident happened on a minor road at Mid Kelton at about 10:30 GMT. Police Scotland said the man was pronounced dead at the scene. 'There are no suspicious circumstances and a report will be submitted to the procurator fiscal in due course,' a spokeswoman said."
So: the incident was at about 10:30 GMT; the BBC published the death at 16:32 GMT; the Guardian headline carrying it went up at 17:10 GMT.

SECOND CASUALTY EVENT — BBC LIVE PAGE, POST TIMESTAMPED 17:27 GMT, by Rachel Grant, BBC Scotland
"Two women have been injured by a falling tree in Aberfeldy, Perth and Kinross, and taken to hospital for treatment. Police have asked people to avoid the Poplar Avenue area of the town near Aberfeldy Footbridge, also known as the 'bouncy bridge', after the incident at about 12:50 GMT."

GUSTS — BBC WEATHER, LIVE POST TIMESTAMPED 13:50 GMT, by Annie Flury, BBC Weather
"The highest recorded so far on Sunday are 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, and 84mph in both Stornoway in the Outer Hebrides, and Capel Curig in north Wales."
Rainfall: Cluanie Inn 130mm; White Barrow 115mm; Affric Lodge 111mm; Honister 97mm; Kinford Gate 91mm; Dyffryn Isaf, Llantrisant 81mm.

POWER — BBC SCOTLAND ARTICLE, VERSION OF 17:15 GMT
"The storm has left more than 50,000 properties without power, with winds gusting to 85mph at Machrihanish in Argyll and Bute."
Scottish Power Energy Networks: "about 6,000 homes in its area are without electricity, mainly across Ayrshire and Dumfries and Galloway", warning more outages could occur.
SSEN: "more than 120 incidents in its area, with hundreds of properties in Aberdeenshire and more than 5,500 homes in the west Highlands without power. Across the network, which covers the north of Scotland, 47,000 customers are awaiting restoration of their electricity supplies and another 32,500 customers have already had their connection restored."
Parts of the Western Isles are on an emergency power station because a link to Skye is down.
6,000 (SPEN) + 47,000 (SSEN) = 53,000, which reconciles with the Guardian's "around 53,000 homes in Scotland... by 5pm".

WARNING TIMINGS — BBC WEATHER ARTICLE OF RECORD (24 Oct)
Amber wind warning, much of Scotland and parts of northern England: 21:00 BST Saturday to 21:00 BST Sunday [the article was written before the clock change; the Sunday end-time is 21:00 GMT].
Second amber warning, parts of the north of Northern Ireland: 21:00 BST Saturday to 10:00 BST Sunday.
Yellow wind warning, Northern Ireland: 10:00 Saturday to 12:00 Sunday.
Yellow wind warning, northern England, north Wales, Scotland: 12:00 Saturday to 21:00 Sunday.
Yellow rain warning, Highlands: 21:00 Saturday to 15:00 Sunday.
Yellow rain warning, south-east to south-west England, Wales, north-west England: 11:00 to 23:00 Saturday.

WARNING STATE THROUGH SUNDAY — BBC LIVE PAGE, POST TIMESTAMPED 15:26 GMT
"The yellow rain warning over northern Scotland expired at 15:00, leaving just two Met Office warnings in place (out of an original six)." Those two are the amber wind warning over most of Scotland and parts of northern England, and the yellow wind warning over the whole of Scotland plus northern England, parts of the Midlands and north Wales. "Both of those expire at 21:00 tonight."

FLOODING — BBC LIVE PAGE, POST TIMESTAMPED 13:34 GMT
England: 4 flood warnings, 49 flood alerts. Wales: 4 warnings, 17 alerts. Scotland: 17 warnings, 11 alerts. "While there's no public data on how many flood related warnings are in Northern Ireland".

SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT — BBC LIVE PAGE, POST TIMESTAMPED 16:49 GMT
Ministers and officials met Sunday afternoon on the "ongoing impact" of the storm. The Scottish government statement says that while conditions may ease later today, "there's potential for adverse weather to return in the coming days".
Social Justice and Housing Secretary Shirley-Anne Somerville "warns travel disruption is likely to continue into tomorrow" and says people should keep up to date on local impacts.
Transport Scotland's Stuart Wilson, quoted: "The weekend of storms has brought challenges across the transport network and, in some cases, there will be significant recovery work required before we have the network back to normal."

TRANSPORT — BBC LIVE PAGE, 15:09 TO 16:01 GMT
Edinburgh Airport: 81 cancelled flights and 11 diversions since the warnings began on Saturday; one flight from Faro diverted to Oslo. Leeds Bradford: more than 20 cancellations. Kirkwall Airport, Orkney, closed until Monday.
Forth Road Bridge closed to all vehicles. Dornoch Bridge (A9) closed to all vehicles. Queensferry Crossing, M90 and Clackmannanshire Bridge (A876) closed to high-sided vehicles with a 30mph limit on other traffic. Kessock Bridge closed to high vehicles. Tay Bridge (A92) cars only on Sunday afternoon. M1 Tinsley Viaduct and A15 Humber Bridge closed to high-sided vehicles. A66 closed between Durham and Cumbria. M8 westbound closed at Junction 8 Baillieston.
Rail: Northern advising against all travel on its network; Avanti West Coast against travel north of Preston; LNER against travel Edinburgh-Aberdeen; TransPennine Express against Liverpool-Manchester and Glasgow-Edinburgh; ScotRail reduced speeds with several routes suspended.
Maritime: an oil tanker 350 nautical miles off the Isle of Mull with 21 people aboard issued a distress alert to HM Coastguard on Saturday afternoon because of "large swells"; an RAF aircraft established communications and it "was determined that there was no need for assistance".
